draft.title: Naming simple organic compounds
card: An IUPAC name has a stem for the number of carbons in the longest chain: meth (1), eth (2), prop (3), but (4), pent (5), hex (6).
The ending shows the bonds or family. -ane means only single bonds between carbons, and -ene means a C=C double bond. -ol means an alcohol, and -oic acid means a carboxylic acid.
A number shows where a feature sits on the chain. Count from the end that gives the lower number. In but-2-ene, the double bond starts at carbon 2.
A halogen on the chain is named as a prefix: chloro, bromo or fluoro. The number shows which carbon it is attached to, as in 2-chloropropane.
draft.remember: Read a name in parts: the stem gives the chain length, the ending gives the bonds or family, and numbers give the position.

a.q: What does the name pent-1-ene tell you about this compound?
opts: Five carbons in the chain and a double bond at carbon 1
Five carbons in the chain and a single bond at carbon 1
One carbon in the chain and five double bonds
Five carbons in the chain and an alcohol group on carbon 1
a.why: Pent means five carbons, -ene means a C=C double bond, and 1 gives its position. The alcohol option is tempting, but an alcohol would end in -ol, not -ene.
a.clue: Split the name into stem, number and ending.

b.q: A compound has a chain of three carbons, only single bonds, and a chlorine atom on the second carbon. What is its name?
b.why: Three carbons gives prop, and only single bonds gives -ane. Chlorine on carbon 2 gives the prefix 2-chloro. Propene is wrong because that ending would mean a double bond.
b.clue: Which ending matches only single bonds?

a.best: Five carbons in the chain and a double bond at carbon 1
